limitations: This estimates sampling uncertainty over tasks/families, not stochastic run-to-run variability.
An observed SE below 1pp is not a guarantee for other models or generator distributions.
Cluster intervals can degenerate when every family has the same result; inspect the Wilson interval too.
The design effect cannot be assumed stable when increasing forms per root or changing task mixtures.
Exploratory construction selection requires separate frozen validation; these intervals do not correct for selection.

implications: At a 60% success rate, independent Bernoulli sampling requires at least 2401 unique tasks for SE strictly below 1pp; at 50%, at least 2501.
Current root-cluster design effects range from about 0.94 to 1.18 in these panels. They are estimates for these panels and cannot safely be carried over to larger repeated-root or paradigm samples.
A two/four-form paradigm is one scored unit. Component counts do not increase the N of all-forms-correct accuracy.

The existing split contains 1000 held-out citation+gana families. An initial design reserved half for a second release; use more of these unqueried families before final freeze if the precision calculation requires it.
Freeze recipe, membership, total planned N or a valid stopping rule, and metric before final responses. Size extensions cannot select harder final tasks.

financial_feasibility.interpretation: OpenAI cannot reserve 5002 maximum-length calls plus discovery within $2000. Verified savings can fund sequential fixed-membership chunks, but no guarantee is made that all chunks fit. No pending/unknown reservation may be released from an assumed average.
financial_feasibility.illustrative_only: At 8000 output and 600 input tokens per request, 5002 batch calls cost about $406.16 Anthropic / $1015.41 OpenAI before discovery and sensitivity. These are scenarios, not observed totals or authorization ceilings.

release_gate: Report IID and root-cluster uncertainty. Do not claim <1pp on the basis of N=1000, repeated completions, component-form counts, or a favorable unvalidated design effect.
